question: An if-statement in Python performs a specified action if a certain condition evaluates to true.
The else clause is mandatory in an if statement in Python.
In Python, multiple conditions can be combined in an if statement using logical operators such as 'and' and 'or'.
The elif statement in Python can be used to specify multiple alternative conditions to an if statement.
In an if statement, if the condition is false, the code inside the if block will be executed.
An if statement can only evaluate expressions of types int and float in Python.
It is possible to nest if statements within other if statements in Python.
The following if statement is correctly written: if x == 10: print('x is 10')
Python allows the use of ternary conditional operators to simplify simple if-else statements, formatted as: x if condition else y.
The indentation level of the code blocks in if statements does not matter in Python.
